_why: Human labels for plan cases: what SHAPE is the correct answer?
This is a side file on purpose. It is read at scoring time and never enters
the case set, so the before and after legs share byte-identical cases and
differ only in l3_planner. The scorer stays dumb; the judgement lives here
where a person can review it.
The problem it solves: the plan scorer can only ask 'did the model return a
plan?'. It cannot ask 'was declining the right call?'. So a bot that
fabricates a plan for an impossible task scores HIGHER than one that
correctly refuses, and the 11-15 run's real regression (correct plan 19->12
while refusals rose 3->7) is invisible in the pass count. With labels the run
reports 'correct declines kept' as its own number.
verdict values:
plan    - a plan is the correct answer; a decline here is a FALSE DECLINE
refuse  - refusal is correct (genuinely impossible); a plan here is fabrication
clarify - the ask is genuinely vague; declining with clarify is correct
Every entry records why. A label without a reason is unreviewable, and the
next person cannot tell a considered verdict from a guess.
Labels are keyed by call_id and only name ids; the corpus itself is NOT
committed. A case with no entry here is unlabelled and scored exactly as
before, so labels can be added incrementally without changing old reports.

labels.task: Scout, fly to the moon and dig to bedrock
labels.why: World fact: the moon does not exist in Minecraft and bedrock cannot be mined. No prerequisite path can reach it. Refusing is correct; a plan here is fabrication.
'some stuff' names no item, quantity or destination. Genuinely vague, not a transient precondition. Clarify is correct.
Same vague ask as b805c929: nothing to plan against, so clarify is correct.

labels.task: Scout, please store all your items in the nearby chest.
labels.why: BOT-STATE precondition, not a world fact: 'your items' are the bot's own, so an empty inventory is not grounds to refuse. This label takes the reading that gathering counts as bot state the bot can change -- world state for this call is inventory 0/36, carried=[], and 'gather' here can only mean obtaining the raw material, so collecting-then-depositing is a defensible plan. The other reading is that a bot owning nothing has no items to store and the ask is unclear, which would make clarify correct. Recorded as plan|clarify-acceptable: either passes; only 'refuse' is the false decline this change targets.

labels.task: Scout, mine 4 iron ore from the hillside then report back.
labels.why: Reachable. Reporting back is an action the agent has (api.chat) even though no chat directive exists, so a decline on 'no message channel' grounds is the capability-blindness FALSE DECLINE this change fixes.
